correctness.rationale: For fixed d>=s>=1, real beta, and positive normalized p_j, checked both directions of polynomial division: deg(P)<=N iff the remainder R=1-(1-t)P has deg<=N+1 and R(1)=1. Distinct homogeneous t^n are orthogonal under the radial total-degree coefficient norm and have exact weights w_n=(n+1)^beta V_n(p). Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives E_N^2=(sum_{n=0}^{N+1}1/w_n)^-1, achieved by unique r_n=(1/w_n)/sum_j(1/w_j). Torus Parseval for V_n has unique maximal phase on its (s-1)-torus; the log-modulus Hessian is A=diag(p_1,...,p_{s-1})-vv^T positive definite with det A=product p_j, giving V_n~(4*pi)^(-(s-1)/2)*product p_j^(-1/2)*n^(-(s-1)/2). For s=1, V_n=1 and the formula follows directly. Positive-series comparison correctly gives the subcritical power, critical logarithm and positive supercritical limit, without assuming uniformity as weights tend to zero. For p=(1/2,1/2), Vandermonde gives V_n=binom(2n,n)/4^n. Independently implemented Fraction-based minimization and determinant/Vandermonde tests across support sizes 1-4 matched formulas; the infinite statement is supported by analytical localization and sum comparisons, not extrapolated from these finite checks.

value.rationale: The fixed-one-generator multiplier class is motivated by the precise 3/2 difficulty of elementary radial Dirichlet cyclicity arguments. The finding determines an intrinsic and sharp barrier of that natural restricted scheme and exhibits an actual interval 3/2<beta<=2 where it fails despite known unrestricted full cyclicity. Its unique finite-N minimizer, exact all-degree errors and unequal-weight support-rank critical exponent give a reusable quantitative diagnostic, not an arbitrary tiny finite slice or mere reformulation of known unrestricted cyclicity. It does not assert the stronger statement about arbitrary multivariate polynomials.

limitations: Strictly positive fixed p_j; no uniformity at degenerating support; only P(t) multipliers, not unrestricted full cyclicity.
